title: Reservoired shadow seeding and dry-run promote orchestrator
author: Avery Cole
description:
Context: We need a safe, reproducible way to seed shadow traffic to new model variants while preserving a bounded surface for automated rollbacks. Current shadow workflows flood a target cluster and can cause noisy telemetry; promoting shadows to canary requires manual validation and replay. This PR implements a 'reservoired' shadow seeding pattern and a dry-run promote command that simulates promote semantics without mutating live routing.

Summary: Adds a reservoir controller that applies a per-cohort budget to shadow traffic, gradual reservoir refill rules, and session-reservation to keep user sessions sticky during a seed. Also implements a dry-run promote operation that performs the promotion decision logic and emits an audit playbook (replay steps, expected traffic fractions, and rollback checklist) but does not change routing. The feature is intended to: 1) reduce blast radius for initial shadow staging, 2) make promote decisions sound and reproducible, and 3) provide an operator-facing playbook for safe manual promotes.

What changed (high level): - New controller: controllers/reservoir_seed_controller.go — owns Reservoir CRD and orchestration logic. - New CLI subcommands: redwoodctl rollout dry-run-promote and redwoodctl rollout apply-reservoir. - Reservoir CRD: api/v1alpha1/reservoir.yaml and typed client scaffolding. - Telemetry: added reservoir.{budget,used,refill_rate} metrics and events for dry-run-audit. - Simulator harness: test/sim/reservoir_sim_test.go for deterministic validation. - Docs: docs/concepts/reservoir-seeding.md and runbooks/rollout-dry-run-playbook.md.

Rollout plan and safety: - Default reservoir budget is 0.5% of cohort traffic and throttle window is 10m. - Session-reservation pins session keys to the shadow variant for up to 5m to maintain fidelity in short interactions. - Dry-run promotes are gated by a metrics gate (latency P95 and failure-rate) and produce an audit artifact stored in the rollout history index (read-only in dry-run). - We added safety checks to refuse direct promote if the reservoir controller detects refill pressure > 85% for > 3 intervals.

Testing: - Unit tests cover controller reconciliation, CRD validation, and CLI flag parsing. - Integration tests run against local kind clusters: the canary-sim pipeline verifies traffic fractions and rollback triggers. - Load bench: we exercised seeding logic under a 10k qps synthetic trace; memory/KV cache behavior verified. - Observability: Grafana dashboard snippets and an alert rule template provided.

Backwards compatibility and migration: - Reservoirs are an opt-in CRD; no change to default routing. - Controllers tolerate older routing objects; feature flag rollout_reservoir seeds off by default. - Migration notes in docs explain how to convert ad-hoc shadow configs to reservoir CRs.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration simulation added - [x] Docs and runbooks added - [x] QA smoke run against staging - [x] Performance bench (10k qps microtrace)

Why this is different: Existing shadow patterns mirror all traffic or rely on ad-hoc throttles. Reservoir seeding treats shadowing as a first-class deterministic primitive with bookkeeping (budget, refill, session-reservation) and a reproducible dry-run promote that lets operators validate the promote decision before changing routing.

Related: Linear ENG-3940, ENG-4021. Jira SUP-721 describes a customer incident where a full shadow swamped a private deployment during a model onboarding window.

review_thread: Maya Singh: Overall this is promising. A few questions on how refill interacts with autoscaling — can refill cause oscillation?
Avery Cole: Refill is capped and uses a leaky-bucket token model; I added notes in reservoir_manager.go and unit tests to show bounded behavior.
Diego Ramos: We should avoid session pinning for >5m by default; customers with long sessions could skew metrics.
Avery Cole: Agreed; changed default to 5m and made it configurable per reservoir CR. Updated docs.
Priya Nair: Observability looks good but add a synthetic smoke alert if reservoir.used grows > 75% for 3 intervals.
Avery Cole: Added alert template and test for alert firing in sim harness.
Maya Singh: CI flake on integration-canary-sim — rerun and passing now. Approved pending one doc nits fix.
Priya Nair: Docs nits addressed, approving.
merge_details: Merged after approvals and green CI. Squash-merge with commit message summarizing reservoir CRD, controller, dry-run promote and docs.
release_notes: Introduces Reservoir CRD and reservoired shadow seeding with a dry-run promote command. Opt-in feature behind feature flag rollout_reservoir=false by default. Adds metrics reservoir.{budget,used,refill_rate} and a runbook for dry-run promotes.
notes_for_operators: 1) To try: enable feature flag rollout_reservoir in staging, create a Reservoir CR with budget 0.005 (0.5%). 2) Use 'redwoodctl rollout dry-run-promote <reservoir>' to generate an audit artifact and validation summary. 3) If validation passes, run 'redwoodctl rollout apply-reservoir' to perform live promote. See runbook path in docs for rollback steps.
